:::{#exm-inner-product-cost}
#### Counting the operations in an inner product

The inner product of two vectors $\vx, \vz \in \reals^D$ is

$$\vx^\top \vz = x_1 z_1 + x_2 z_2 + \cdots + x_D z_D.$$

Computing it takes $D$ multiplications, one for each product $x_d z_d$,
and $D - 1$ additions to sum the $D$ products:
$2D - 1$ arithmetic operations in all.
Since $2D - 1 \le 2D$ for every $D \ge 1$,
the cost is $O(D)$, with $D$ in the role of $n$, $c = 2$ and $n_0 = 1$ in @def-big-o.
Since $2D - 1 \ge D$ for every $D \ge 1$, it is also $\Omega(D)$,
so it is $\Theta(D)$.
When a machine learning text says an inner product "costs $O(D)$",
it means this count of operations, up to a constant factor.

:::
